title: Two acquisitions bracket Zurich’s record nine-month update
full_text:
Zurich Insurance Group posted nine-month P&C gross written premiums of US$42.1 billion in its Q3 2026 trading update, up 7% on a like-for-like basis. Asia Pacific was one of the stronger regional performers, with P&C GWP growing 9%, led by the retail motor and commercial middle market segments, aided by expanding digital partnerships.
Australia was specifically cited in the release as a contributor to international commercial GWP growth, alongside Canada, Italy and Spain, as that segment grew 3% across the nine months. The release does not break out Australian or New Zealand GWP separately, but the call-out confirms the region contributed to outperformance in Zurich’s commercial book even as overall commercial rates fell 1%.
Overall P&C rates rose 1%, driven entirely by the retail segment, which was up 4%. Commercial insurance rates fell 1%, primarily because of the large property segment where Zurich is explicitly “selective on the business written” in softer conditions. Outside property, the release flags “initial indications of slower decline” in US financial lines and cyber, a signal that the downward rate trajectory in those lines may be stabilising globally.
For Australian and New Zealand brokers placing commercial property risks, the cat loss ratio in the release is worth noting. It rose to 3.2% for the nine months, up from 1.4% in the prior-year period. Elevated Q3 losses were concentrated in the retail Europe segment following severe storms across Switzerland, Germany and Italy, and the Colombia earthquake. No Australian or New Zealand events are cited individually in the release.
The nine-month update lands against two completed transactions that materially change Zurich’s footprint in Australia. Zurich Financial Services Australia completed the AU$385 million acquisition of ClearView Wealth on August 20, adding a third adviser-distributed life insurance brand alongside its existing Zurich and OnePath Life products.
According to specialist research house Dexx&r, the acquisition gives Zurich approximately 23% of Australia’s advised life market. This is an adviser-channel transaction rather than a broker-channel one, but the consolidation of life insurance ownership in Australia’s retail market is a structural development the broader intermediary channel will monitor.
Separately, the Beazley acquisition closed October 1, one day after the nine-month reporting period closed. The combined specialty book is expected to write approximately US$15 billion in GWP globally. For Australian brokers placing large commercial and specialty risks through Beazley’s Lloyd’s syndicates, Kristof Terryn has been named chief executive officer of the combined entity, subject to regulatory approval. Adrian Cox has departed as Beazley’s CEO. How the combined entity’s appetite evolves across specialty lines will become clearer through the next renewal cycle.
Zurich’s Swiss Solvency Test (SST) ratio stands at 271%, up from 266% at the half year. This is a trading update, not a full results release. No combined ratio or operating profit is included.
